title: Complete summary – Urinary tract: kidneys, ureters & bladder
html:
Built by reverse-engineering every MCQ of this lecture. 🔁 = asked in several sessions · ⚠ = classic trap.

Normal kidneys

  • Length 10–12 cm, located T12–L2, left slightly higher and ~1.5 cm longer (the right is NOT always longer); cortex visible on US.

Techniques 🔁🔁

KUB plain film

  • Shows radiopaque stones, calcifications, renal outlines, psoas lines. NOT function, NOT a "mute" kidney, NOT uric-acid stones (radiolucent).

Intravenous urography (IVU / IVP)

  • Iodinated contrast i.v. → nephrogram then pyelogram; shows the collecting system.
  • Irradiates the gonads – protection IS possible ⚠
  • Plain film before contrast → stones; 5-min film → morphology and symmetric excretory function (calyces); later films → ureters, bladder.
  • Functional mute kidney: no contrast in the pelvis at 5 AND 15 min and no contrast in the ureters.
  • Not all stones visible; not the most sensitive test.

Renal ultrasound 🔁🔁

  • First-line, cheap, non-invasive; gives MORPHOLOGY only – NO functional information ⚠
  • Shows hydronephrosis, differentiates cyst vs solid mass and hydronephrosis vs cysts; useful for complications of acute pyelonephritis; superior to IVP for masses.
  • Not for staging renal cancer (= CT); cannot rule out urolithiasis (misses ureteral stones).

CT phases of the kidney (asked in 2022, 2023 AND 2025) 🔁🔁🔁

PhaseTimingCortex / medulla
Native–same density
Arterial = corticomedullary25–40 sSEPARATE (cortex brighter) – the ONLY phase
Nephrographic90–100 shomogeneous – best for masses
Late / excretory5–10 minhomogeneous; contrast in calyces
  • "Same density" → native, nephrographic, late, excretory (all except corticomedullary).

Scintigraphy

  • Dynamic (DTPA/MAG3): obstruction (diuretic renography), split function, renovascular hypertension (captopril). Static DMSA: cortical scars / acute pyelonephritis. NOT stones.

Urolithiasis 🔁

  • Most sensitive: non-contrast (low-dose) CT – gold standard, confirms stones in symptomatic patients; almost all stones (incl. uric acid) hyperdense.
  • US: echogenic focus with acoustic shadow, but cannot rule out lithiasis.

Kidney size syndromes 🔁🔁🔁

SMALL kidneyLARGE kidney
Chronic pyelonephritis (scars), nephrosclerosis, renal artery stenosis, (congenital) hypoplasia, chronic nephritis, end-stageAcute pyelonephritis, hydronephrosis, acute renal vein thrombosis, polycystic disease, tumour (polar / extensive)
  • Typical trap: "small kidney is NOT produced by" → renal vein thrombosis, polar tumour, polycystic kidney, hydronephrosis. "Large kidney cannot be produced by" → chronic pyelonephritis.

Cysts & tumours

  • Bosniak (CT): I simple cyst (no follow-up, no biopsy), II, IIF follow-up, III indeterminate (surgery), IV enhancing soft tissue (malignant).
  • Adult polycystic disease: bilateral; contrast does NOT enter the cysts. (Solid isthmus in front of the aorta = horseshoe kidney.)
  • Renal cell carcinoma: solid enhancing cortical (exophytic) mass, can calcify, invades renal vein and IVC → vascular assessment looks for a venous tumour thrombus; staging = CT (single best method to assess a renal tumour); does NOT contain fat.
  • Angiomyolipoma: the ONLY renal tumour diagnosed accurately by US + CT – hyperechoic on US, macroscopic fat (negative HU) on CT. Oncocytoma cannot be separated from RCC.
  • Urothelial carcinoma (urothelioma): starts in the renal sinus, filling defect in the collecting system, spreads "along the watershed" (urothelium), multicentric, may calcify. Venous thrombosis and extrarenal spread = RCC.
  • FALSE statements (2025): "MRI is the method of choice in any suspicion" ✗ (CT; MRI = problem solving); "only arteriography gives the diagnosis" ✗ (obsolete); "urothelial tumours best detected by scintigraphy" ✗.

Bladder stasis 🔁🔁

CompensatedDecompensated
Detrusor hypertrophy, wall thickening, trabeculation, pseudodiverticulaAtonic, LARGE thin-walled bladder, large residue

Kidney transplant – colour Doppler

  • Preferred for: renal artery stenosis, fluid collections, acute tubular necrosis / rejection (resistive index), urinary obstruction. NOT: lymphoproliferative disease, stones (= CT).
